title: Tenant-aware eviction allocator with atomic lease handoff and auditable correctness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching increases request concurrency and KV cache use, eviction decisions can cause correctness regressions (stale KV hits, prefix leakage across tenants, and transient OOMs on GPU). We need a hybrid eviction allocator that composes LRU + TTL + prefix affinity while providing atomic handoff semantics for in-flight requests and an auditable trail for correctness validation.

Goal: Design and ship a tenant-aware eviction allocator that: (1) prevents serving requests from stale/evicted KV entries, (2) ensures prefix-scoped isolation so one tenant's eviction policy doesn't evict another's hot prefixes, (3) avoids turning short-lived spikes into large-scale cache churn under continuous batching, and (4) provides determinable invariants we can test and monitor for production correctness.
design_decisions: Hybrid score: eviction rank = w_lru * lru_score + w_ttl * ttl_score + w_affinity * prefix_cost, configurable per-tenant and per-shard to tune fairness vs cost.

Lease handoff: implement short-term leases for KV slices. A lease must be acquired before demotion; holders serving in-flight batches keep a soft pin until batch completion. Lease acquisition is atomic at shard-level via compare-and-swap on a lease epoch counter.
Prefix affinity groups: group keys by prefix fingerprint and maintain watermarks to avoid evicting >X% of a prefix's entries in a single window; prefix affinity is tenant-aware.
Grace period for continuous batching: when observed sequence of requests indicates high reuse, extend TTL for pinned prefixes using adaptive hysteresis rather than immediate LRU penalty.
Fallbacks: when eviction would cause GPU memory pressure beyond threshold, trigger a fast-path demote-to-host (CPU) for least-recently-used slack pages instead of hard evicting pinned prefixes.
Auditability: emit immutable eviction events with (shard, prefix_hash, epoch, reason, chosen_candidate_keys) and attach request traces for postmortem and property checks.
invariants: I1: No request may be served from a KV slot after an eviction event for that slot has been committed with epoch >= slot_epoch.
I2: Prefix isolation: eviction decisions must not reduce cached entries for any prefix below its configured min_reserve unless global memory pressure > emergency_threshold.
I3: Lease atomicity: at any point, a slot's lease epoch monotically increases; any lease-holder observes epoch >= at-acquire and can serve until batch_end without seeing an older epoch.
I4: Demotion determinism: demotion -> allocation must preserve that demoted pages are not reinserted into the same slot without going through a revalidation flow (sequence number check).

acceptance_criteria: AC1: All invariants I1-I4 have passing automated checks in the fuzzbench harness over 100k synthesized request sequences.
AC2: Telemetry for eviction events and lease transitions are present in prod traces and stored for 30d (schema validated).
AC3: Under a synthetic continuous-batching workload, eviction churn rate reduced by >=40% vs baseline while tail latency meets SLOs.
AC4: No incidents of cross-tenant prefix leakage during canary traffic (canary window: 72h, 10% traffic).
AC5: Rollout gating: feature flag enabled; must be manually approved after canary metrics meet thresholds.
test_plan: Unit: lease epoch CAS, scorer math edge cases (zero weights, extreme TTLs).
Integration: end-to-end with batch router + runtime to ensure in-flight batches retain valid KV pins.
Fuzzing: property-based tests asserting invariants across random sequences of gets/prefetch/evict/demote with multiple tenants and bursty rates.
Performance: stress with continuous batching traces from production (sampled), measure churn, GPU mem high-water, and request tail latency.
Chaos: simulate delayed lease release and verify safety fallbacks and demotion path behave without data corruption.
monitoring: Metrics: eviction_count_by_reason, eviction_churn_rate, lease_acquire_latency, lease_conflicts_per_min, demote_to_host_count, prefix_watermark_violations
SLOs: tail latency P99 < 120ms for cache hits under target load; GPU mem headroom > 8% in steady state.
Alerts: prefix_watermark_violations > 5 in 10m, lease_conflicts spike > 100/min, demote_to_host_count > threshold
Dashboards: per-tenant eviction heatmap, prefix-reserve utilization, and per-shard lease epoch drift.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag per-cluster. Stages: (1) Canary cluster with synthetic and 10% traffic for 72h; (2) Expand to non-critical customers at 25% for 7 days; (3) Full roll with automatic rollback on breach of canary thresholds. Maintain manual abort path. Prior to full roll, run migration job to compute prefix watermarks from historical access traces to seed min_reserve values.
